steps.title: Cut the metal: plate + 2 links (printed jig)
steps.how: Base: 1/8" aluminium sheet, 120 x 110 mm, holes drilled through a printed template. Links: two pieces of 1/8" x 1/2" flat bar. Drop each one in the printed drill jig and drill both 4.0 mm (5/32") holes through it: the holes come out exactly 42 mm apart on both links. A parallelogram only stays level if the two links are identical, so the jig is the key part.

steps.title: Tower + turntable servo + bearing on the plate
steps.how: The printed tower screws onto the plate with 4 M3 screws. The MG90S goes inside (2 tab screws) and the 6807 presses into the top. Two stacks of steel washers on M6 bolts are the ballast. They replace the old printed cups and sand.

steps.title: Turret + shoulder servo (MG996R)
steps.how: This is A2's turret with one addition: an ear above the servo for the second link's pivot. Melt an M3 heat-set insert into the ear with a soldering iron. Plastic threads wear out; brass ones don't.

steps.title: Parallelogram: metal horn + 2 links + coupler
steps.how: This is the EEZYbotARM idea. The 25T aluminium horn clamps onto the MG996R spline, and link A bolts to it with 2 M3 screws. Link B pivots on the ear. Both links pin to the printed coupler with M3 shoulder screws into heat-set inserts. The coupler carries the wrist servo.

steps.title: Claw (unchanged)
steps.how: The same gripper frame, gears, fingers and SG90 as now.

steps.title: Lift: the can rises without tilting
steps.how: The MG996R swings link A from -10.7° to +10.7°, and link B follows. Because the links are equal and parallel, the coupler translates and doesn't rotate: the can rises 15.7 mm and stays level. In A2 it tilted 7.1°. The swing is symmetric, so the can drifts less than 0.7 mm forward or back. Watch it in ▶.

report: CAN LANDING: centre (127.0, 0.0), upside down 180.0 deg, bottom z -0.0 -> PASS
COLLISIONS through the firmware sequence (every 4th of 289 poses): PASS (none)
LIFT: links swing -10.7 -> +10.7 deg, can +15.7 mm (>= 15.2), can tilt while lifted 0.00 deg (A2: 7.1), forward drift 0.74 mm mid-stroke, 0.00 at the top -> PASS
SHOULDER (MG996R): load 71 g; a parallelogram's driven link only sees the load x the pin distance (41 mm), not the CG's (90 mm): 0.64 kg*cm with 2x dynamic vs 9.4 stall: 7 % -> PASS
PIVOT LOAD: the overhang moment goes into the links as push/pull: 0.9 N per pin (91 g) vs ~600 N an M3 shoulder screw in aluminium takes -> PASS
TURNTABLE (MG90S): 0.020 kg*cm to accelerate vs 1.8 stall: 1.1 % -> PASS
TIP-OVER (with the 2 x 60 g washer stacks): CG -2 mm toward the front edge at 38, 15 mm toward the side edge at 60 -> PASS

PRINT TIME, same profile: A (as built) 21 h 53, A2 (redesign) 9 h 03, D (hybrid) tower 3h 24m 17s, turret 3h 26m 48s, coupler 43m 59s, link_jig 36m 5s = 8 h 09 (63 % less than A; claw the same in all three)
